chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Abu Ja'far, from Sa'd ibn Isma'il ibn Isa, from his father, who said: I asked Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who became junub in the month of Ramadan and slept intentionally until morning, what is upon him?

He said: This does not harm him, he does not break his fast, and he is not concerned, for my father (peace be upon him) said: Aisha said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) became junub from intercourse, not from wet dream.

Because it carries two meanings: one is that it was a way of exiting through taqiyya (dissimulation), for that is the narration of the general public from Aisha, and for that reason he (peace be upon him) also narrated it from her, and did not narrate it from his fathers (peace be upon them).

And if it were sound, the correct view in it is: that whoever sleeps intentionally and his sleep continues until the rise of dawn, nothing is incumbent upon him. Rather, the qada (making up the fast) and kaffarah (expiation) are incumbent upon the one who intentionally leaves the ghusl, not the one who intentionally sleeps. And in the report it is not stated that he intentionally left the ghusl.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one sleeps intentionally while junub in Ramadan without breaking the fast?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Rida, who clarifies that intentional sleep while junub does not invalidate the Ramadan fast, distinguishing it from the obligation of kaffarah which applies only to intentionally delaying ghusl. The Imam supports this by citing the general report of the Prophet becoming junub from intercourse (not just nocturnal emission) and interpreting it through the lens of taqiyya, thereby establishing that mere continuity of impurity until dawn incurs no penalty.
